question: Horizon Europe: legal basis for the suspension announcement of 4 March 2022

On 22 October 2025, the Commission stated that the measures announced on 4 March 20221 concerning the suspension of cooperation with Russian entities and of payments to those entities, as well as the decision no longer to sign new contracts with Russian entities under Horizon Europe, were based on EU restrictive measures and Horizon Europe eligibility restrictions2.

However, as previously pointed out, those provisions were adopted after the March 2022 decision3. In its subsequent reply, the Commission no longer referred to those provisions. Instead it referred to subsequent ‘relevant legal measures’ and ‘far-reaching restrictive measures’, ‘adopted subsequently’ to 24 February 2022, without identifying the precise legal basis for the March 2022 decision4.

The fifth sanctions package, adopted on 8 April 2022, gave the Commission the competence to terminate the participation of Russian public bodies or publicrelated entities in ongoing Horizon Europe projects. 1.

Regarding the suspension of cooperation with, and payments to, Russian entities under Horizon Europe, can the Commission identify the specific legal provision in force on 4 March 2022, which gave it the competence to act?

Regarding the March 2022 decision no longer to sign new contracts with, and to suspend payments to, Russian entities, can the Commission confirm that this was an executive decision taken on its own authority?
